item.title: 1958: Boston Red Sox Outfielder Jackie Jensen, Who Hit .286
item.description: Boston Red Sox outfielder Jackie Jensen, who hit .286 with 31 home runs and 122 RBI, is named American League MVP, winning over Cy Young Award recipient and World Series MVP Bob Turley and Cleveland Indians outfielder Rocky Colavito (.303, 41, 113). Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 2024: Naile Re–signed With the Tigers on a $1
item.description: On November 26, 2024, Naile re–signed with the Tigers on a $1.

item.title: 2024: Vitale Was Hired by the Miami Marlins as a Bench Coach
item.description: On November 26, 2024, Vitale was hired by the Miami Marlins as a bench coach. Photo: Jacob Sippel (Public domain).

item.title: 2015: Snyder Signed a Minor League Contract
item.description: On November 26, 2015, Snyder signed a minor league contract with the Atlanta Braves organization. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2008: Hankyu Nishinomiya Gardens, a Shopping Mall Containing a Hankyu
item.description: Hankyu Nishinomiya Gardens, a shopping mall containing a Hankyu Department Store, an Izumiya supermarket, Toho cinemas, and dozens of smaller clothing, fashion, and food outlets, was opened on November 26, 2008, on the vacant lot where the stadium used to be. Photo: 投稿者(Cake6 (talk))がスキャナ (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2007: The Lotte Giants Hire Jerry Royster as Their New Manager. Royster
item.description: The Lotte Giants hire Jerry Royster as their new manager. Royster, a former major league player and longtime minor league manager, is the first foreigner ever hired to manage a team in the Korea Baseball Organization. Another Lotte-owned team, the Chiba Lotte Marines, of Nippon Pro Baseball, had had their best run ever thanks to an American manager, Bobby Valentine. Photo: San Diego Padres (Public domain).

item.title: 2006: Báez Signed a Three-Year Deal With the Orioles on November 26, 2006
item.description: Báez signed a three-year deal with the Orioles on November 26, 2006. Photo: User Keith Allison on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2004: Vladimir Guerrero, Who Hit .337 With 39 Home Runs and 126 RBI
item.description: Vladimir Guerrero, who hit .337 with 39 home runs and 126 RBI, earned the American League MVP Award, while receiving 21 of the 28 first-place votes. The former Montreal Expos outfielder had signed as a free agent with the Anaheim Angels after the New York Mets refused to guarantee his salary based on advice from their medical staff. Photo: Derral Chen from Los Angeles, U.S.A (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2003: Hoping to Add Punch to Their Lineup
item.description: Hoping to add punch to their lineup, the Oakland Athletics trade catcher Ramón Hernández and disgruntled outfielder Terrence Long to the San Diego Padres in exchange for outfielder Mark Kotsay. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2002: Prior to Playing Two Regular-Season Games Against the Oakland
item.description: Prior to playing two regular-season games against the Oakland Athletics to open the major league season in Japan, the Seattle Mariners will face the Seibu Lions and Yomiuri Giants in exhibition contests on March 22 and 23 of spring training. Photo: MC2 Jerry Jimenez (Public domain).

item.title: 1999: Arbitrator Alan Symonette Rejects the Owners' Attempt to Dismiss
item.description: Arbitrator Alan Symonette rejects the owners' attempt to dismiss the umpires' grievance, giving the 22 booted umps a chance to get their jobs back. Symonette will hear the grievance beginning December 13.

item.title: 1997: Fletcher Signed as a Free Agent
item.description: Fletcher signed as a free agent with the Toronto Blue Jays on November 26, 1997. Photo: Best Cards (Public domain).

item.title: 1996: Less Than Three Weeks After Major League Owners Vote 18-12 Against
item.description: Less than three weeks after major league owners vote 18-12 against ratification of baseball's new collective bargaining agreement, owners vote again and this time approve it by a vote of 26-4. The landmark agreement brings interleague play to the regular season for the first time as well as revenue sharing among owners and a payroll tax on players.

item.title: 1986: The New York Yankees and Pittsburgh Pirates Work out a Six-Pitcher
item.description: The New York Yankees and Pittsburgh Pirates work out a six-pitcher, interleague trade in which the Yankees send Doug Drabek, Logan Easley and Brian Fisher to Pittsburgh for Pat Clements, Cecilio Guante and Rick Rhoden. Drabek, 24, will win 22 games and the NL Cy Young Award as a Pirate in 1990. Photo: flickr user James G (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1985: The California Angels Retain the Services of 16-Year Veteran Second
item.description: The California Angels retain the services of 16-year veteran second baseman Bobby Grich, 36, granted free agency November 12. On December 5, the Angels will also return free-agent pitcher and future Hall of Famer Don Sutton, 40 and a 20-year veteran, to the fold. Photo: Baltimore Orioles (Public domain).

item.title: 1975: Boston Red Sox Center Fielder Fred Lynn Becomes the First Rookie Ever
item.description: Boston Red Sox center fielder Fred Lynn becomes the first rookie ever to be named American League MVP. Lynn, who hit .331 with 21 home runs and 105 RBI, also posted league-leading figures in runs (103), doubles (47), and slugging (.566), helping Boston to the American League East title. He also won Rookie of the Year honors. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1965: Los Angeles Dodgers Second Baseman Jim Lefebvre, Who Hit .250
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers second baseman Jim Lefebvre, who hit .250 with 12 home runs and 69 RBI, is voted National League Rookie of the Year over Houston Astros second baseman Joe Morgan (.271, 14, 40) and San Francisco Giants pitcher Frank Linzy (9–3, 43 strikeouts, 1.43 ERA). Photo: Ticketron (Public domain).

item.title: 1960: Upon Arrival in the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and Saint Paul
item.description: Upon arrival in the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and Saint Paul, the team formerly known as the Washington Senators chooses the appropriate nickname Twins as its new identity. Photo: Washington Senators (1901-1960) (Public domain).

item.title: 1957: Yoshio Tanaka, an American Citizen of Japanese Descent
item.description: Yoshio Tanaka, an American citizen of Japanese descent, is named manager of the Hanshin Tigers, becoming the first American to manage a NPB club.

item.title: 1954: Bill Doak, 63, Pitcher for Three Different Clubs in a Span of Sixteen
item.description: Bill Doak, 63, pitcher for three different clubs in a span of sixteen seasons from 1912 to 1929, eleven of them with the St. Louis Cardinals, who won 20 games in 1920 and twice led the National League in ERA in 1914 and 1921. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).

item.title: 1950: The Gillette Safety Razor Co. Signs a Six-Year Deal
item.description: The Gillette Safety Razor Co. signs a six-year deal, worth an estimated $6 million, with Major League Baseball for the television and radio rights for the World Series.

item.title: 1949: In Japanese Baseball, the Central League Is Joined by the Pacific
item.description: In Japanese baseball, the Central League is joined by the Pacific League. Photo: Mr.ちゅらさん (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1948: National League President Ford Frick Steps
item.description: National League president Ford Frick steps in and pays $350 for funeral services, including the cost of a coffin, for the unclaimed body of former Chicago Cubs slugger Hack Wilson, who led the NL in home runs four times between 1926 and 1930, and in the latter year bashed 56 homers (an NL record that stood for 68 years) and drove in 191 runs (still the MLB RBI all-time record). Photo: J. G. Taylor Spink (Public domain).

item.title: 1935: The National League Assumes Control of the Bankrupt
item.description: The National League assumes control of the bankrupt, Boston Braves franchise after several failed attempts to buy the last-place club. The league takes over only temporarily, until matters can be straightened out.

item.title: 1912: John T. Brush, 67, Owner of the New York Giants From 1902 Until
item.description: John T. Brush, 67, owner of the New York Giants from 1902 until the time of his death, who also owned the Indianapolis Hoosiers in the late 1880s and the Cincinnati Reds from 1891 to 1902. Photo: George Grantham Bain Collection (Library of Congress) (Public domain).

item.title: 1909: The Philadelphia Phillies Are Sold for $350,000 to a Group Headed
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies are sold for $350,000 to a group headed by sportswriter Horace Fogel. Because of his dual roles, Fogel will become the only executive barred from a league meeting. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1891: A Series for the Championship of the Pacific Coast Begins Between
item.description: A series for the championship of the Pacific coast begins between the champions of the California League (the San Jose Dukes) and the Pacific Northwest League pennant winners (the Portland Webfeet). San Jose wins the opener, 8–6. The series will last until January 10 with San Jose winning 10 games to 9. All the games are played in San Jose, California.

item.title: 1886: Albert Spalding of the National League Champion Chicago White
item.description: Albert Spalding of the National League champion Chicago White Stockings sells his 2nd starter within a week in his attempt to rid the team of players who drink alcohol. Photo: George Grantham Bain (Public domain).
